# What a finite closed cover transfers from an empty supporting face

Let K be a d-dimensional convex body, d>=1, and let H_1,...,H_N be
closed halfspaces whose traces cover K. The same conclusion below holds
if they only cover K up to d-volume zero. Let

    J_+={j:|K intersect H_j|_d>0}.

Then the positive-volume traces alone cover the ENTIRE body:

    K subset union_(j in J_+) H_j.                       (1)

Indeed, a cap of zero captured volume cannot contain a point of int K:
any halfspace containing such a point has positive volume in K, even
if the point lies on its boundary. Thus every interior point is covered
by the positive-volume members. In the almost-everywhere formulation,
their finite closed union covers int K as well: an uncovered interior
point would have a neighborhood missing this union, while the remaining
zero-volume caps cannot cover that positive-volume neighborhood.
The finite union is closed, and closure(int K)=K, proving (1).

Suppose H_i is an empty supporting cap: |K intersect H_i|_d=0, but
its face F_i=K intersect boundary H_i has positive H_(d-1) measure.
Then (1) gives, for every nonnegative measurable function w on F_i,

    integral_(F_i) w dH_(d-1)
      <=sum_(j in J_+) integral_(F_i intersect H_j) w dH_(d-1). (2)

The assertion includes d=1, when F_i is a point of H_0 measure one.
It excludes i and ALL other locally empty caps from the recipients,
even when their boundary hyperplanes coincide with F_i. Thus (2)
is not an artifact of closed caps covering each other's null faces.

For an ambient mixed cover, apply the lemma in each actual positive
fiber. A vertical restriction is either the whole fiber or empty and
causes no difficulty. In particular one may take
w=dist(h(z,x),[0,1]), the weight occurring in orientation-resolved
equality-cap flux. However the recipient caps need not belong to the
positive circuit through a given pair of candidate centers. The finite
global cover may use different caps at that external fiber.

## Coverage does not compare recipient section measures

There is no universal estimate replacing the traces on the right of
(2) by a constant times the recipients' OWN section measures, even
for a planar triangle. Take

    K=conv{(-1,0),(1,0),(0,-1)},
    H_0={y>=0},
    H_+={y>=-1+epsilon},
    H_-={y<=-1+epsilon},       0<epsilon<1.

H_0 is empty in area and its supporting face F_0 has length 2.
The two positive-area caps H_+,H_- cover the whole plane, and hence K.
Their common proper section through K has length 2epsilon, so the sum
of their own section lengths is 4epsilon. The face F_0 is entirely in
H_+ and disjoint from H_-. Thus the trace on the right of (2), with
w=1, has length 2, whereas the putative recipient-section substitute
is 4epsilon. Their ratio tends to infinity as epsilon decreases to zero.
The exact cap areas are 1-epsilon^2 and epsilon^2, respectively.

The three continuous normals (0,1),(0,1),(0,-1) even have the positive
balance with coefficients 1,1,2, so that weak additional property alone
does not supply a section-measure comparison. They are not asserted to
form a minimal common-contact critical circuit, nor to arise at a
global mixed-depth plateau. The example therefore obstructs only an
inference from coverage and positive normal balance alone. It does not
refute a stronger estimate using genuinely minimizing caps, small mixed
budgets, common endpoint data, or further compatible-fiber geometry.
